text:
alex: heads-up: deploybot blocked the staging -> prod promote for gcr://redwood/apps/payment because the manifest list has duplicate linux/amd64 entries with different digests. Publishbot flagged provenance mismatch.

-devops-bot: [automated] Promotion halted by policy: manifestlist_platform_duplication. See logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/gh/4231 :warning:

-tina: ugh. does this mean some clients will pull the wrong digest? :eyes:

-jess: likely yes for multiarch-aware clients — they pick the first matching platform entry. If the ordering differs between mirrors, people can end up with different image digests.

-marco: how widespread is staging? is canary already on prod?

-alex: canary rollout is at 12% in eu-west and us-central, those pods already pulled the new manifestlist. non-canary clusters are still on the previous digest (pinned).

-priya: options: 1) rollback canary (pull older pinned digest) 2) pin the canary nodes to the older digest while we republish a corrected manifestlist 3) retag offending digest as new tag and republish (but provenance flags might block).

-jess: retagging won't change the manifestlist duplication if the manifestlist itself is wrong. We can create a new manifestlist with correct platform ordering + cosign sign, but that requires republish which touches provenance/audits.

-alex: immediate mitigation: pin the canary deployment to the previous confirmed digest to stop variance. Then schedule a republish of a corrected manifestlist in the maintenance window (tonight 00:30-01:30 UTC).

-devops-bot: action created: INFRA-9873 "Pin canary to previous digest and prepare corrected manifestlist republish" assigned to alex, jess, priya.

-marco: agree with pin. if we rollback the canary pods they'll restart pulling the pinned digest? what's the command?

-priya: run:

```
kubectl set image deployment/payment-canary payment=gcr.io/redwood/apps/payment@sha256:1111aaaa2222bbbb3333cccc4444dddd --namespace=canary
```

That will force pods to pull the pinned digest.

-alex: i'll run that now and watch health checks.

-jess: parallel task: i'll prepare the corrected manifestlist using crane and cosign:

```
# assemble manifest list with ordered platforms
crane manifest create --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 gcr.io/redwood/apps/payment:staging-fixed sha256:1111... sha256:2222...
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/keys/payment-manifest gcr.io/redwood/apps/payment:staging-fixed
```
We need approval from release-manager before pushing to prod registry.

-release-manager: approved to republish to staging and run canary again in maintenance window. Do not push to prod until we confirm provenance checks pass. Update release notes with the incident and the pin decision.

-tina: for release notes, add explicit note: "Staging manifestlist duplication caused heterogeneous pulls; canary pinned to previous digest; corrected manifestlist scheduled for republish in maintenance window; no customer-facing rollback required."

-priya: one more: confirm mirrors (eu mirror and us mirror) will have identical manifest order after republish. Use a propagation check script after push.

-jess: will run propagation checks and post results. If any mirror shows inconsistent ordering, we'll hold full promote and triage.

-alex: pinned canary now. health looks ok (no errors in logs). thanks. I'll kick off the republish playbook at 00:35 UTC.

-devops-bot: [automated] INFRA-9873 status update: canary pinned -> success. Next step: pre-publish checklist scheduled for 00:35 UTC.

-marco: thanks — remind infra oncall 30m before window.

-release-manager: noted. also add a one-line entry in the changelog for tonight's release: "Fix manifestlist platform ordering for payment image; tested propagation and provenance checks." :shipit:

-alex: filing a postmortem stub to capture root cause and why publishbot allowed duplicate entries in the manifestlist. link: https://pm.internal/incidents/INFRA-9873

-priya: TL;DR: mitigation = pin canary; republish corrected manifestlist in window; run propagation & provenance checks; then promote.

-jess: i'll attach the exact crane/cosign commands and the propagation-check script to the ticket for runbook reuse.

-alex: good. closing thread for now, we'll post updates after the window. :thumbsup:
